correctness.rationale: Chaudhary–Gupta's equations (1.2), (1.7) and (3.2) fix both the density 4uSf and the unscaled subtraction J(U_{2,2})−J(X). With u=−log S and du=h dx the kernel is g(u)=exp(−2u)/2−8u²exp(−4u); its integral is zero. Here h=a+b1_{u≥q}, q=aτ, so integrating only the excess-hazard tail gives Δ/b=[exp(−2q)−(1+4q+8q²)exp(−4q)]/4. The logarithmic derivative of exp(2q)/(1+4q+8q²) changes sign once from negative to positive at (1+√3)/4; the ratio starts at one and tends to infinity, proving the unique positive, transverse crossing. The derivative of Δ/b has the sign of 16q²−exp(2q); exp(q)/q has minimum e at 1, and the two roots give the stated Lambert W extrema with both endpoint limits zero. Independent bisection and evaluations gave q*=1.731442936471895, q−=0.357402956181389, q+=2.153292364110349, normalized extrema −0.0842524983427735 and 0.00124826711558150, and magnitude ratio 67.49556828910. For the smooth family h=a+bℓ_k(u−t), the inverse of x=∫du/h exists analytically across every finite point of the half-line, tends to infinity, and gives a proper density with physical-time hazard derivative h'(u)h(u)>0. The logistic-minus-step L¹ error on the full line is 2 log(2)/k, so the contrast converges uniformly in t with the stated bound. Opposite signs at t=1 and 2 give existence by continuity; the simple step root gives convergence and the O(1/k) rate for the roots chosen there.
residual_risks: Only the population contrast is zero. The record does not establish a sampling power, rejection-probability or distributional equivalence theorem, or uniqueness for finite logistic steepness.

value.rationale: An exact, robust counterexample to identification by a specific published scalar contrast is meaningful within the natural IFR model class. The threshold, signs and very unequal extremal magnitudes describe precisely where that contrast distinguishes or misses a simple lifetime alternative, and the analytic construction rules out an explanation based on a discontinuous hazard.
residual_risks: This does not determine the empirical test's power; extending the result beyond this population contrast would require new analysis.
